title: Deeper/broader consumer-policy and directionality cross-check

sources.finding: DWG import is opt-in and read-only; the documented source contract prevents saving over the DWG and directs Save As to a new file. This is product policy, not parser conformance evidence.

DWG import is converter-to-DXF followed by a selected DXF importer. Automatic selection tries LibreDWG, ODA, then QCAD; the LibreDWG branch treats output-path existence as success without checking the subprocess return code.
Broad read-version coverage coexists with advanced-class and writer limitations; some unknown types are retained as binary data without DXF codes. Capability must be scored per direction and type.

The xref/copy operation can ignore unsupported ACAD_TABLE and preserved unknown-tag entities without raising; this limitation is operation-specific and cannot be generalized to ordinary document read/write.

plan_delta: Add a negative LibreCAD_3 consumer-policy assertion: opening DWG must leave source bytes unchanged, prohibit overwrite, and route Save As to a new DXF.
Keep FreeCAD native qualification bound to the effective converter and importer; independently validate converter process status, output DXF, and final document semantics.
Keep per-operation outcomes distinct: read, rewrite, cross-document copy/xref, projection, and export.
